page: Amazon Web Services trn2.48xlarge is a high-density instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor offering 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated virtual CPUs running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. It includes 2048.0 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 10.67 GB of RAM per physical core, suited for large-scale memory-bound enterprise operations.

For local data handling and communication, the instance features 7600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, providing high direct disk I/O throughput. Baseline network throughput is rated at 200 Gbps, enabling rapid data transfers across cluster environments or distributed systems. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, trn2.48xlarge delivers substantial memory capacity and fast attached storage bundled within a single instance footprint. This density minimizes the necessity of scaling out across multiple nodes for datasets requiring single-node memory structures. A notable architectural tradeoff in this specific configuration is the absence of discrete GPU accelerators, shifting compute reliance entirely onto its 192 dedicated CPU threads and memory subsystem. Primary workload fits include large in-memory databases, data processing pipelines, enterprise backend software compilation, and IO-intensive storage hosting.
